extra.message: The username parameter from the query string is interpolated directly into the SQL query string using an f-string on line 182: f'SELECT * FROM users WHERE username = "{username}";'. This untrusted input passed to run_sql_query which executes via db.execute(query) (line 146) without any parameterized binding. An attacker can inject arbitrary SQL, e.g. via ?username=admin%27%20OR%201=1-- to bypass authentication or extract data.

The PUT /user endpoint (lines 188-204) interpolates all six User model fields directly into an SQL INSERT query via f-string: user.name, user.username, user.password, user.address, user.email, and user.contact. All values are passed to run_sql_query which executes via db.execute(query) (line 146) without parameterized binding. An attacker can supply crafted values in any field to inject arbitrary SQL statements.

The DELETE /user endpoint interpolates the username parameter directly into an SQL DELETE statement via f-string on line 231: f'DELETE FROM users WHERE username = "{username}";'. The value goes through run_sql_query which executes without parameterized binding. An attacker can drop any record or perform SQL injection.

The DELETE /user endpoint also interpolates user.address directly into an SQL DELETE statement on line 235: f'DELETE FROM users WHERE address = {user.address};'. Notice the address value is NOT quoted, meaning it bypasses simple quote-escaping techniques but still suffers from injection since the value is concatenated unsafely through the f-string and passed to run_sql_query without parameterized binding.

The GET /find endpoint passes the username query parameter directly to users.find() on line 220 as a MongoDB-style dictionary: {'username': username}. This untrusted input is used to construct the NoSQL query without any validation or sanitization. An attacker can inject MongoDB operators (e.g., {"$gt": ""}) to enumerate all records, bypass lookups, or exploit operator injection.

The POST /find endpoint reads the entire request body from await request.json() on line 224 and passes it directly to get_nosql_users() which calls users.find(query) on line 171. An attacker can craft arbitrary MongoDB query operators in the JSON payload to enumerate all documents, inject $where clauses for JS code execution, or bypass filters.

The POST /reset endpoint (lines 243-247) completely wipes both SQL and NoSQL databases via remove() and rmtree(), then re-initializes them with empty schema. There is zero authentication, authorization, or CSRF protection on any route. Any unauthenticated caller can destroy all application data by simply sending a POST request to /reset.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: The get_nosql_users function (lines 169-174) returns raw user records from the NoSQL database to the API caller. Although it removes '_id' and 'password' fields on line 172, all other personal data (name, address, email, contact) is returned directly as JSON. Any authenticated or unauthenticated user can enumerate and exfiltrate PII by querying the /find endpoints.

User passwords are hashed using MD5 via hashlib.md5() on line 187. MD5 is cryptographically broken and unsuitable for password hashing — it is extremely fast to brute-force and vulnerable to collision attacks. A proper implementation should use bcrypt, argon2, or scrypt with per-user salts via a library like passlib.

cwe: CWE-916: Use of Hashed Password With Insufficient Computational Cost

extra.message: The seed data generation in init_sql_db (lines 101-121) uses faker library to generate random users with real-looking names, addresses, emails, phone numbers, and passwords. The generated password hashes are written directly to the database as f-string values on lines 110-117. While these are seeded records, this demonstrates the same SQL injection pattern (CWE-89) since all faker-generated values are interpolated unsafely into SQL queries.
